findings.text: Header exposes a family of small helpers for huge-page cgroup accounting covering charging and committing charge for normal and reserved pages, uncharging folios, cgroups, file regions and counters, plus lookup and install of the owning cgroup on a folio, duplication and release of reservation uncharge state, file subsystem init, and migration of state between folios.

In the configuration shown, the huge-page cgroup facility reports itself disabled, lookups from a folio yield a null owner, charge attempts report success without storing an owner, and all commit, uncharge, set, file-init, migrate and reservation-info helpers have no observable effect.

Fork and exit handling for the huge-page collapse daemon is conditional on an address-space flag: when the source or current space carries the huge-page flag the operation delegates to a separate enter or exit routine, otherwise it does nothing; the alternate configuration makes fork, exit, VMA entry, collapse, and free-threshold update no-ops and reports the current task as never being the daemon.

Available collapse-daemon integration points are per-address-space fork and exit hooks, a per-VMA entry hook taking VMA and flags, a collapse helper taking address space, address and install flag, a free-threshold refresh helper, and a predicate testing whether current context is the daemon.

A zero page table entry is recognised by combining a zero frame test with a dirty bit test; mapping a zero page increments both a global and a per-address-space counter, unmapping decrements both only when the entry matches, and a reader returns the per-space count.

An address space joins or leaves merging based on flags: fork propagates mergeable state from parent to child while resetting merging and rmap counters and folding the child zero count into the global count before entering, exec enters only when a merge-any flag is set, and exit leaves only when mergeable is set; the disabled configuration leaves all these transitions as no-ops with success status.

When the merging feature is unavailable, VMA flag adjustment is identity, disable and madvise report success, fork, exit, zero-page unmap, reverse-map walk and folio migration helpers do nothing, folio copy check returns its input, and the out-of-memory collection helper is empty.

Soft leaf entries distinguish a none value, ordinary swap, three migration modes for read, read-exclusive and write, device-private read and write plus device-exclusive, hardware-poison, and a generic marker class.
The bit position where the soft-leaf type number starts is defined to be the same position used for swap type numbers.

A swap-style value packs a type number in high bits and an offset in low bits under a mask; dedicated extractors recover the type by shifting down and the offset by masking, and constructors translate between abstract entries and architecture PTE or PMD slots through arch-specific encode and decode steps.

Conversion from a PTE or PMD to a soft leaf yields none when the source is present or empty; otherwise it strips swap-only flag bits for exclusivity, soft-dirty and userfaultfd state before arch decoding and repacking, with one PMD configuration unconditionally yielding none or a zero PMD on the reverse path.
In the configurations shown, soft-dirty queries for swap PTE and PMD always report clear and the corresponding clear operation is identity.

Classification treats a zero-valued entry as none, decodes the type number by shifting, treats numbers below the configured swapfile limit as ordinary swap, maps specific reserved numbers to migration, device, poison and marker classes depending on build options, and treats any other number as unknown with a one-time warning collapsing to none.

Single-purpose predicates test for swap, each migration mode, device-private write, device-exclusive, poison and marker, while grouped predicates report any migration state or any device-private read-or-write state.

Marker payload is obtained by masking the offset; poison, guard and write-protect markers test individual bits only after confirming marker class; migration young and dirty states test offset bits only when access-dirty emulation is supported, otherwise they report false, with a second configuration that always reports false.

Only migration, device-private, device-exclusive and poison entries are defined to carry a frame number subject to a build-time width check; the frame number is the masked offset, and page or folio resolution converts that number through the frame-to-page mapping.

Migration entries may only be examined while the associated folio is locked, enforced by a read barrier plus a warning on unlocked use; extracting a frame, page or folio without the pfn property warns, classifying an unknown type warns once, and resolving a PMD folio from an invalid entry warns and yields null.

PTE conveniences detect any marker, write-protect markers, and userfaultfd-handled markers covering write-protect and poison; PMD conveniences detect device-private and migration entries with one device-private configuration always false; only device-private and migration classes count as valid PMD soft leaves, and PMD folio resolution validates before converting.
A memory policy object holds a reference count, mode and flag shorts, a node mask, a home node integer, a union of either cpuset-allowed nodes or user-supplied nodes, and an RCU callback head.
A shared policy holds a red-black root plus a read-write lock, and each interval node holds tree linkage, start and end offsets, and a pointer to a policy object.
The shared-policy container co-locates a read-write lock with its interval tree root.

Policy references are optional-pointer safe: put and duplicate delegate when non-null, plain get increments the count, conditional helpers test a shared flag before putting, identity implies equality while distinct pointers delegate to a deep comparison.

In the configuration shown, control and seal queries report invalid-argument failure, folio and file allocation report error pointers for invalid argument, and seal validation for mapping reports success without effect.
The anonymous memfd display label is the fixed bracketed memfd name.
The no-interleave index sentinel is the all-ones unsigned long value, directing interleaving to use the task previous position.
